summary: Other: 他人, other people; 他山, another hill. Its use as the pronoun “he” came later.
placement: Chosen by farthest-point sampling on the integrated Burke–Shaw trajectory, so the eight stars spread across its projected shape. 遠 takes the point farthest from the system’s centre, 孤 the most isolated of the rest, and 寂 the point nearest the centre. A design choice, not a claim.

satellites.title: Stones from Another Hill
satellites.evidence: The Odes, Heming: 他山之石，可以為錯 … 他山之石，可以攻玉 — “stones from another hill can serve as a whetstone … stones from another hill can work jade.” What shapes us comes from elsewhere.

satellites.title: When the Other Became “He”
satellites.evidence: Classical 他 means other: 他人, other people; 他山, another hill. Later it became the third-person pronoun for anyone, and in the early twentieth century writers split it into 他, 她 and 它, he, she and it.
satellites.caveat: The coinage of 她 is usually credited to Liu Bannong (c. 1920); dates and credit are from general knowledge.
gaps: Cite a history of the 她 coinage.
